Immune checkpoints in Alzheimer disease (AD)

a, Several AD risk genes modulate the immune suppression mediated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) that is observed in cancer biology. Several of these genes were reported to promote myeloid cell transition to MDSCs197,201,207,213,215,217,218,221,222,234,263,264,283,347–349, while others were associated with inhibition of MDSCs191,193,283. In addition, several cytokines that are altered in AD can modify MDSCs: interferon-γ (IFN-γ) reduces MDSCs193, while interleukin-34 (IL-34) increases CD163-expressing MDSCs195. The downstream effects of AD risk genes in MDSCs include checkpoint upregulation (programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) or TIM3 (also known as HAVCR2)) in MDSCs, neutrophils or dendritic cells (DC)191,199,207,221,264,348,350, metabolic alterations (such as reduced glucose metabolism, which has been linked with increased formation of regulatory T cells (Tregs)137,151,154,213,223, and increased immunosuppressive cytokine secretions (including interleukin-10 (IL-10) or transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)) in MDSCs, which can prevent T cell activation207,214,218,351. b, Elevated levels of programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte protein 4 (CTLA-4) in aging and AD drive T cell exhaustion225; Antibody-mediated blockade of PD-1 or its ligand, PD-L1 (not shown), restored IFNγ-driven Aβ clearance by monocyte-derived macrophages in 5xFAD mice and promoted T cells to convert into active effector T cells57. Follow-up studies however reported opposite effects of targeting PD-1 in AD mice226 and/or no changes in monocyte recruitment to the CNS or improvement of Aβ-plaque pathology227,228. c, CD33 variants linked to AD risk impair Aβ clearance; The CD33M long isotype deletion increases pathology and impairs cognition, while the CD33m short isoform enhances Aβ compaction243,244. Using liposomes or antibodies to target CD33 offer therapeutic potential by removing the blocking of INPP5D (downstream of CD33) on the TREM2 pathway and thereby promoting Aβ degradation245. d, Expression of TIM3, which signals via TGFβ, on mature microglia inhibits Aβ clearance, positioning TIM3 as a promising target for microglial activation in AD53
